Statement: Σ₂P ⊄ SIZE(nᵏ) for every fixed k
Notes: Win-win on whether NP ⊆ P/poly.

Statement: Either P ≠ NP or E ⊄ SIZE[2ⁿ/n]
Source / proof: If P = NP then Σ₂E = E by padding; Σ₂E ⊄ SIZE[2ⁿ/n] is Chen–Hirahara–Ren 2023 (arxiv.org/abs/2309.12912)
Notes: Hardness conservation: hardness sits in NP (against algorithms) or in E (against circuits).

Statement: E ⊄ SIZE[2ⁿ/n] (near-maximum circuit lower bound for E)
Source / proof: Follows from P = NP via L02
Notes: Would give BPP = P (Impagliazzo–Wigderson 1997). Technique tags describe the P = NP-side derivation.

Statement: BPP = P
Notes: Conjectured in every world; would follow from L03.

Statement: P ⊄ SIZE(nᵏ) for every fixed k
Source / proof: L01 plus the collapse PH = P
Notes: Best unconditional circuit lower bounds for P are only linear.

Statement: NP ⊆ P/poly (SAT has polynomial-size circuits)
Source / proof: Immediate under P = NP; Karp–Lipton 1980 for consequences
Notes: Refuting it (NP ⊄ P/poly) proves P ≠ NP: the circuit-lower-bound route. Crypto worlds with non-uniform security would set it False.

Statement: Universal search finds SAT witnesses in polynomial time on satisfiable inputs
Notes: Never halts on unsatisfiable inputs; the equivalence is for the search version.

Statement: PH = P
Notes: PH = P iff P = NP.

Statement: Nested SAT, fixed instances, polynomially many levels, answer bits used as literals (P^NP) is in P
Notes: With negative occurrences allowed this problem is P^NP-complete.

Statement: Nested SAT where every answer bit occurs only positively stays in NP
Source / proof: NP is closed under ∧, ∨ and monotone substitution
Notes: B[a] is satisfiable iff B[0] is satisfiable, or A is satisfiable and B[1] is satisfiable.

Statement: Depth-k nested SAT whose inner formulas depend on outer variables (Σₖ) is in P, for each fixed k
Source / proof: Σₖ ⊇ NP; PH collapses under P = NP
Notes: Depth-k parameterized nesting is Σₖ-complete.

Statement: TQBF ∈ P (polynomial-depth parameterized nesting; PSPACE = P)
Notes: Under P = NP the exponent compounds with depth (roughly n^(c^d)), so P = NP does not obviously give P = PSPACE. Mirror of L27.

Statement: SAT ∈ DTISP(nᶜ, n^o(1)) for some c < 2cos(π/7) ≈ 1.8019
Notes: Constrains Algorithmica (SAT is not near-linear in tiny space) without contradicting it. 2cos(π/7) is the proven ceiling of alternation-trading proofs.

Statement: NEXP ⊄ ACC⁰
Notes: Algorithmic method: circuit-SAT faster than brute force implies lower bounds. Commonly described as avoiding the relativization and natural-proofs barriers; tags not yet checked against the paper.

Statement: S₂E ⊄ SIZE[2ⁿ/n]
Notes: Pigeonhole made explicit through range avoidance. The authors state the proofs relativize. S₂E is far above NP.

Statement: One-way functions exist
Notes: Liu–Pass: one-way functions exist iff Kᵗ is mildly hard on average.

Statement: Public-key encryption exists
Notes: Defines Cryptomania.

Statement: Some NP problem is hard on average (distributional NP ⊄ AvgP)
Notes: Heuristica is worst-case hard but average-case easy.

Statement: MCSP ∈ P (a P-natural property useful against P/poly exists)
Notes: One-way functions give pseudorandom functions, and a fast MCSP algorithm would distinguish them from random.

Statement: R(Kᵗ) ∈ P for every polynomial t
Source / proof: Evaluation doc, Prop. 3.2; HILL 1999 (one-way functions give PRGs)
Notes: A PRG's outputs have low Kᵗ, so deciding R(Kᵗ) breaks every PRG.

Statement: R(Kᵗ) is P-immune (Lemma B of the evaluated argument)
Notes: The unproven step of the 'Pseudorandom Trap' argument.

Statement: R(K) is immune (no infinite c.e. subset)
Notes: Classical.

Statement: No Kolmogorov-random finite strings exist
Notes: At least 2ⁿ − 2ⁿ⁻ᶜ + 1 strings of length n are c-incompressible.

Statement: Chaitin: a consistent Σ₁-complete theory proves 'K(x) > L_T' for no x
Notes: Limits proof, not existence.

Statement: NP-intermediate problems exist
Notes: Under P = NP every NP language is in P, so none are intermediate.

Statement: No sparse set is NP-complete (Karp reductions)
Notes: Under P = NP the sparse set {1} is NP-complete.

Statement: P ≠ PSPACE
Notes: Mirror of L12.

Statement: Every satisfiable formula A has a satisfying assignment x with Kt(x | A) = O(log n)
Notes: If P = NP, a search algorithm running in nᵏ steps outputs a solution, so Kt(x | A) ≤ k·log n + O(1). Conversely, universal search finds such a solution in polynomial time and rejects after the budget, deciding SAT.

Statement: Direct product for verifiable SAT search: if every randomized short program solves at most 1 − δ₀ of D_m in time m^k', then every short program solves r = C ln m independent blocks with probability ≤ 2e^(−γr)
Source / proof: Impagliazzo–Jaiswal–Kabanets 2009 (weakly verifiable puzzles); CLAUDE DIRECTPRODUCT-0001, Thm 3R
Notes: Randomized black-box reduction. The deterministic uniform version needs L30.

Statement: Lemma 2 of the direct-product note: a deterministic polynomial-time seed list hits every short program's dense success set for all but 1/m of any samplable distribution
Notes: Implies one-sided heuristic derandomization of RP over samplable distributions; IW98 gets only infinitely-often subexponential simulations from BPP ≠ EXP. If P = NP, approximate counting makes the list constructible. The note's proof is FALSIFIED/RETIRED.

Statement: Some samplable distribution on satisfiable formulas has SAT search hard on average for every polynomial-time randomized algorithm
Notes: This is the direct-product note's hypothesis at every budget. Minicrypt/Cryptomania: inverting a one-way function as planted SAT. Heuristica is probably False via average-case search-to-decision; left Open until checked.

Statement: Portfolio collapse: one constant-size algorithm simulates every program of length ≤ b₀ + d·log N with an O(N^d) time factor, so common defeating instances at budget N^k follow from SAT-search lower bounds at time N^(k+d+o(1))
Notes: Shows the direct-product route to the UWI common-input statement is dominated: it needs only worst-case hardness and loses only d in the exponent.

Statement: T-PORT: SAT ∉ ∃^(log N + b₀) DTISP(N^c, N^o(1)) for some c > 1 (UWI portfolio lower bound in small space, decision form)
Notes: Decision form (an N-bit witness does not fit in small space). Alternation trading cannot reach it: see L34 (barrier) and L36. Collapse plus Williams gives only c < 0.80.

Statement: Barrier: no alternation-trading proof in system S (Williams Speedup Rules 1–2, portfolio slowdown leaving a residual of width d·M, free absorption, brute force) refutes SAT ∈ ∃^(d log N)DTS[N^c] when c ≥ 1 and c + d ≥ 2
Notes: At d = 1 (UWI portfolio) nothing beyond the trivial c < 1; at d = 0 it is Williams' quadratic barrier. A statement about proofs, so true in every world.

Statement: For 0 ≤ d < 1 and c(c+d) < 2: SAT ∉ ∃^(d log N)DTISP(N^c, N^o(1)); computer-found proofs give more, e.g. (d,c) = (9/10, 21/20), (3/4, 57/50), (1/2, 261/200)
Source / proof: CLAUDE TPORT-0001, Thm 4 and exact replay (verify_exact.py)
Notes: Sublinear portfolios admit nontrivial bounds; d = 1 is exactly the threshold. Beats the collapse bound 2cos(π/7) − d for d ≥ 1/2.

Statement: The L34 barrier still holds when Skolemization (∀r∃z ≡ ∃(z_r)∀r, table merged into the previous block) is added to S
Notes: COMPUTATIONAL: 0 of 47,938 proofs of length ≤ 18 beat c = 1 at d = 1; Skolemization never improved any exponent. Two natural potentials fail; proof open.

Statement: Asymptotic threshold: the best exponent c*(d) provable by the S rules satisfies 1 + (1−d)/3 ≤ c*(d) ≤ 1 + (1−d) on [0,1], and c*(1−ε) ≥ 1 + (29/50)ε for all small ε > 0
Source / proof: CLAUDE TPORT-0002 (closed form; barrier; exact ε-polynomial certificate of a length-22 proof)
Notes: So the provable gain over linear time is Θ(1 − d) and vanishes linearly at the UWI size. Exact cost match: one speedup round trip changes time by at least c(t−x) + dx − t. The limiting slope lies in [0.58, 1]; its value is open.

Statement: Every one-tape Turing machine, deterministic or nondeterministic, deciding 3-SAT (clause-list encoding) needs Ω(N²/log N) time on infinitely many lengths
Source / proof: Owner's note (equality family F_{a,b}); CLAUDE ONETAPE-0001 Thm 1; Hennie 1965; Santhanam IPL 2001
Notes: Crossing sequences. Tight for nondeterministic one-tape machines up to polylog (NTIME_1(SAT) = O(N² log² N)), so the method cannot separate determinism from nondeterminism.

Statement: Sequential-access portfolios: SAT needs T·S = Ω(N²/log N) on off-line machines with sequential input, for deterministic portfolios of up to 2^{Ω(N/log N)} programs and for on-the-fly nondeterminism
Notes: So the UWI small-space portfolio statement (L33) holds with exponent up to 2 when input access is sequential; with random access, alternation trading cannot exceed 1 (L34). The difference is the input-access model.

Statement: SAT needs one-tape deterministic time N^(2+δ) for some δ > 0
Notes: Would imply a superlinear deterministic multitape lower bound for SAT, which is open. Crossing-sequence counting is capped at O(N²).

Statement: Bridge(Res): SAT ∈ P ⟹ W̄_Res(N) ≤ poly(N), where W̄_R(N) = max over UNSAT F with |F| ≤ N of the minimum refutation size in R (best sequence free)
Source / proof: CLAUDE BRIDGE-SQUEEZE-0001 Thm 2; Haken 1985 (W̄_Res superpolynomial unconditionally)
Notes: Because W̄_Res is unconditionally superpolynomial, the bridge is false if P = NP and vacuously true otherwise. The same holds for every system with a known superpolynomial lower bound (tree-like and general resolution, cutting planes, polynomial calculus, bounded-depth Frege). A bridge for such a system is P ≠ NP restated.

Statement: Bridge(EF): SAT ∈ P ⟹ W̄_EF(N) ≤ poly(N) for Extended Frege (also for the project calculus R_mix341, which contains ER_2)
Source / proof: CLAUDE BRIDGE-SQUEEZE-0001 §4; Cook 1975; LSPV-1 357 (true when some P-time SAT algorithm has a PV-provable rejection-soundness proof)
Notes: Vacuous if P ≠ NP. Proving it outright means proving P = NP ⟹ EF p-bounded, which is open. Bridges move up under p-simulation (Lemma 1), so stronger systems have easier bridges.

Statement: LB(EF): W̄_EF(N) is superpolynomial (no polynomial-size Extended Frege refutations for some UNSAT family)
Notes: Not implied by P ≠ NP and not known to fail if P = NP. Together with L42 it would give P ≠ NP. This is the lower-bound half the boxed program needs for any system strong enough to have a non-trivial bridge.

Statement: NP ≠ coNP, equivalently W̄_R superpolynomial for every Cook–Reckhow system R
Notes: This is what a lower bound on minimum derivation cost with free best sequence proves when it holds for all R. Free choice of sequence makes W̄_R a nondeterministic measure, so the all-R version is stronger than P ≠ NP.
